questions.q: Several users report the instance "feels slow." Why shouldn't that be treated as confirmed proof of a platform-wide problem?
options: ServiceNow instances can never actually be instance-wide slow
Users experience the platform through whatever they personally use, so a degraded feature they all happen to share can feel universal even if nothing else is affected
User reports are always fabricated and should be ignored entirely
Only developers are allowed to report performance issues
questions.explain: A loud, widely-used feature that's degraded produces the same first report as a genuine platform-wide event — triage exists to tell them apart.

questions.q: What is the first step in triaging a reported platform-wide slowdown?
options: Immediately roll back the most recent deployment
Restart the instance without gathering any evidence
Open a ServiceNow Support case before checking anything internally
Confirm the scope is genuinely instance-wide using the Instance Health Dashboard, rather than assuming the report is accurate as stated
questions.explain: Instance Health answers the trend-level, instance-wide question first — before any fix is attempted for either a platform event or a narrower issue.

questions.q: After Instance Health confirms a genuine instance-wide slowdown, what should be checked next, and why?
options: Whether a recent deployment correlates in time with when the slowdown started, since a change affecting every transaction is the most common real cause
Whether any user has ever submitted a complaint before, regardless of timing
The color scheme of the Service Portal, since that's unrelated but easy to check
Nothing further is needed once Instance Health confirms the scope
questions.explain: A deployment correlated in time with the slowdown's start is the fastest hypothesis to test and the most common real cause of a sudden, instance-wide degradation.

questions.q: If there's no correlated deployment, what should be checked for resource exhaustion, per this lesson?
options: The exact wording of the original user complaint, repeated verbatim
Semaphore and node usage, since a runaway scheduled job or genuine capacity pressure can produce the same instance-wide symptom with a different fix
Whether the Slow Request Log has ever been opened before
The number of active UI Policies on the Incident table only
questions.explain: Semaphore exhaustion or genuine node capacity pressure need a different fix (killing/rescheduling a job, or addressing capacity) than rolling back a bad deployment.

questions.q: Why does this lesson insist on gathering evidence through all three steps before attempting any fix?
options: Because ServiceNow Support requires three pieces of evidence before opening any case
Because fixes are never actually needed once evidence is gathered
Because a bad deployment, a runaway job, and genuine capacity pressure look identical to users but require completely different responses
Because the Instance Health Dashboard cannot be used more than once per day
questions.explain: Each candidate cause produces the same symptom from a user's chair, so acting on a guess risks applying the wrong fix to the wrong root cause.
